drug_class: Lymphocyte function-associated antigen-1 (LFA-1) antagonist / anti-inflammatory eye drop
purpose: Lifitegrast is used to treat dry eye disease in adults. It helps relieve the signs and symptoms of dry eyes, such as eye discomfort, irritation, and blurry vision. Your doctor may prescribe it if your eyes feel dry, gritty, or uncomfortable on a regular basis.
how_it_works: Dry eye disease involves inflammation on the surface of your eyes. Lifitegrast works by blocking certain proteins in your immune system that trigger that inflammation. By reducing the inflammatory response, it helps soothe and protect the surface of your eye over time.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include a temporary stinging or burning sensation when you put the drops in, eye irritation or redness, blurred vision right after using the drops, eye discharge, and an unusual taste in your mouth or throat shortly after use. Most of these effects are mild and tend to get better as you continue treatment.
warnings: Do not wear contact lenses while putting in the drops — wait at least 15 minutes before reinserting them. Lifitegrast is for use in the eyes only; never swallow it. Tell your doctor if you experience severe eye pain, worsening redness, or any signs of eye infection. Let your doctor know about all other eye drops or medications you are using to avoid interactions. Safety has not been established in children under 17.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one drop in each affected eye, twice a day — roughly 12 hours apart (for example, morning and evening). Use it regularly every day for the best results, even if your symptoms start to improve. It may take a few weeks to notice the full benefit.
